exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal delivery vs cesarean section)
outcome: Diversity and composition of the intestinal microbiota
cohort: 41 newborn infants (25 vaginal deliveries and 16 cesarean sections)
finding: Delivery method significantly influences the structure of the intestinal microbiota in Chinese newborn infants, with vaginal delivery associated with a predominance of Escherichia coli, Bacteroides sp, and Bifidobacterium longum, while cesarean section is associated with more Staphylococcus sp, Clostridium sp, Enterobacter sp, and Streptococcus sp.
mod_finding: Cesarean section is associated with a different gut microbiome composition compared to vaginal delivery.
